paragraphs.text: Claude Code plugin: recap any session's intent, key decisions, changes, open threads and where to re
sume, in a side pane. Built for long, many-session projects.
# session-recap
English | 中文
Remember what every AI coding session was for.
intent · key decisions · what changed · open threads · where to resume, for sessions of any length,
from any agent, through MCP, a local viewer or a plugin
Projects grow, and so does the number of sessions in each one, often across several agents. After a
few weeks a session is a 100 MB transcript you no longer remember: why you started it, what you deci
ded, what was left half done.
**session-recap** reads a session's whole transcript and writes a short, structured recap. Use it fr
om **any MCP client** (Codex, Cursor, Zed, Cline, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Claude Code…), in a **local
viewer** for every agent's sessions, from the **command line**, or through native plugins for **Clau
de Code**, **dsh** and **Codex**.
| Section | What it answers |

| **Intent** | What was I ultimately trying to achieve? |
| **Key ideas and decisions** | What did w

e choose, and why? Which alternatives were rejected? |
| **What changed** | Files, features, documen

ts, commits, PRs |
| **Open threads** | What is unfinished, unverified or still a question |
| **Whe
re to resume** | The most sensible next step today |
Every recap also has a **Map**: the phases the work went through (pivots marked) down to "you are he
re", the key decisions with what was turned down, and lists of what shipped, what is open and what w
as dropped. Recaps are written in the language you mostly write in.
## Quick start
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then, in your agent: *"Recap this session"*, *"What was my last session in this project about?"*, *"
ur agent: *"Recap this session"*, *"What was my last session in this project about?"*, *"总结一下这个会话"*.
**No API key needed.** Through MCP, the agent you are talking to writes the recap with its own model
; session-recap only reads and condenses the transcript. A model of session-recap's own is optional
(for the CLI and the viewer's **Write recap** button).
Or run it without installing: `npx session-recap …`. session-recap has no dependencies and runs no i
nstall scripts. The development version: `npm install -g github:BruceXcluding/session-recap --allow-
git=all` (npm 12 blocks installs from GitHub without the flag).
**Requirements:** Node.js 20+, `python3` (macOS ships one), and for dsh sessions the `zstd` command
* Node.js 20+, `python3` (macOS ships one), and for dsh sessions the `zstd` command or Python 3.14+.
## Ways to use it
| | Best for | How |

| **MCP server** | any MCP client | `session-recap mcp-config <client>`, see below |
| **Local viewe

r** | browsing every agent's sessions, Recap and Map | `session-recap serve` |
| **Claude Code plugi
n** | a Recap / Map pane beside the chat | `/plugin install session-recap --marketplace BruceXcludin

g/session-recap` |
| **dsh plugin** | `/recap` and the `session_recap` tool in dsh | packages/dsh |

| **Codex plugin** | the MCP server, packaged for Codex | plugins/codex |
| **Command line** | scrip
ts, quick looks, other formats | `session-recap`, `session-recap list` |
### MCP server
`session-recap mcp-config <client>` prints the entry for `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini` (and
Qwen Code), `opencode`, `zed`, `vscode` or `cline`, with absolute paths so an IDE started from the d
ock finds it. For example:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Tools:
| Tool | What it does |

| `list_sessions` | Sessions of every agent, filtered by title words, project folder or agent |
| `r
ecap_session` | The recap of the current session (or one named): a stored one if the session has not
changed; else written by session-recap's model if one is configured; else the condensed, secret-fre

e transcript and instructions for the calling agent to write it |
| `save_recap` | Stores the recap
the agent wrote, so it is reused, and updated from the new part next time |
`recap_session` also takes `format`: `standup`, `handoff` or `pr` instead of the recap.
### Local viewer
`session-recap serve` opens `http://127.0.0.1:4711` with every agent's sessions by project folder, g
rouped by time, filtered by agent; each session's Recap and Map; and, with a model configured, **Wri
te recap** and **Update recap**. It reads the recaps written by the Claude Code plugin, the CLI and
MCP clients alike. It answers only on loopback, to the browser tab it opened.
### Claude Code plugin
`/session-recap` recaps the session you are in; `/session-recap browse` lists projects and sessions;
`/session-recap <name>` opens a project or a session by name. The pane shows Recap and Map, uses th
e session's own model (or one picked under **Model**), and shows your Claude Code sessions first, wi
th **All agents** one tap away.
### Command line
| Command | What it does |
| `session-recap [words]` | Recaps the session whose title holds the words; with none, the newest on

e in this folder |
| `session-recap list [words]` | Lists sessions (the calling agent's; `--all` for

every agent) |
| `session-recap --format standup` | A standup note instead (`handoff`, `pr`) |
| `s
ession-recap --dry-run` | Shows the size that would be sent, and how many secrets were removed, with

out calling a model |
| `session-recap models` | Lists your provider's models |
[该节后续省略]
## Privacy
- **Local.** Sessions are read on your machine. Text leaves it only in the model call a recap needs:

your agent's (MCP, plugins) or the one you configured (CLI, viewer). No telemetry.
- **Secrets remo
ved first.** Keys, tokens, private keys, credentials in URLs and `PASSWORD=…`-style assignments are
replaced with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` before any text reaches a model. `--dry-run` shows how many. It is

pattern matching, so it cannot know every format: see SECURITY.md.
- **What is sent** is a condense
d transcript: your prompts, each turn's final reply, commits and PRs, the files edited. Tool output
and intermediate replies are left out.
